model: FCFE at cost of equity, managed-care insurer (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL cash-flow statement add-back (ShareBasedCompensation), FY2025 10-K. Cash taxes on net-share settlement not separately captured in the XBRL pull; at 0.19% of revenue SBC is immaterial to the valuation and the omission is well inside rounding.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q3 2026 10-Q cover: 120.10m shares outstanding at 30 Sep 2026, plus ~1.4m dilutive awards (Q3 diluted weighted average 121.83m against a basic weighted average of ~120.4m; the dilutive count rose with the share price) = 121.5m fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Buybacks remain token ($110m in 9M 2026, $2.7bn of authorisation unused) while capital is retained for MA growth and margin repair.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flows are FCFE (post-interest net income less equity retained for statutory capital). USD build: 10y UST ~4.2% + 0.95 beta x 5.0% ERP = ~9.0%. Beta is set above HUM's historical ~0.6 because the earnings stream is now dominated by a single regulator's annual decisions (CMS rate notice, Star Ratings, RADV); the same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios so risk is charged once, in the scenario weights, not twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: None required. Operating leases (CenterWell clinics, offices) are inside GAAP pretax income via rent expense; no lease liability is added to net debt because net debt is held at zero on the FCFE route.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material NCI. Net income is attributable. The October 2026 BlackRock/HPS joint venture (~150 CenterWell clinics, BlackRock majority, CenterWell minority with operating control) removed the WCAS put option; the related fair-value gains (Q3 2026 other income of $358m, and the ~$1.2bn net put liability reversal booked in Q4) are non-cash and are excluded from the margin path. CenterWell's call options on the JV clinics from 2028 are discretionary and are not in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE capitalised at cost of equity, run through the owner-FCF engine with net_debt = 0 (same precedent as IAG.AX and GL, which override the dcf-methods default of BVPS-compounding for insurers that do not compound book: HUM equity went $16.1bn FY21 to $17.7bn FY25 with $4.7bn of buybacks in between and ~$10bn of it is goodwill). Model unchanged from the 2026-09-29 valuation. Why not owner-FCF at WACC: Humana's OCF is swung by CMS prepayment timing (Q3-22 +$8.5bn, Q1-23 +$6.7bn, FY25 only $0.9bn against $1.2bn net income), the $20bn+ investment portfolio backs statutory reserves and cannot be treated as surplus cash, and subsidiary dividends to the parent are capped by RBC rules, so the distributable flow is net income less statutory capital retained. ENGINE MAPPING: ebitda_margin_path = GAAP pretax margin (ex non-cash put/call fair-value items) + sbc_pct, so that after the engine deducts SBC the line is pretax income (already after interest expense, $607m in 9M 2026, and including investment income on the reserve portfolio, which is operating float income and NOT stripped; the portfolio is correspondingly not added to the bridge, per the matching-asset rule). da_pct = 0 and capex_pct = 0 because D&A and capex are inside pretax margin; wc_capture_pct = -5 models equity retained for statutory capital at ~5% of incremental revenue. The $12.5bn holding-company debt is charged through interest expense in pretax income, so net_debt is 0 in the bridge; deducting it would double-count. cash_tax_rate 24% = HUM's normal GAAP effective rate; no NOL shelter. last_fcf = FY2025 FCFE proxy = net income $1,203m less 5% x $11,903m revenue growth = $608m, NOT reported_fcf - sbc (that figure, $134m, is CMS-timing noise). ANCHORS: FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); year 1 = FY2026 with three quarters reported; balance sheet and share count from the Q3 2026 10-Q (30 Sep 2026). PRICE: the Yahoo regular close at inputs.price_as_of sits roughly 17% below the 52-week high set after the October Star Ratings release; HUM_Analysis.json describes the stock as above $450 in mid-November, which the quote no longer supports, so treat the Analysis price commentary as stale. FY2026 (re-judged): 9M 2026 revenue $121.7bn (+25.5% YoY) and Q4 at the Q3 run-rate gives ~$162bn, so base year-1 growth is 25% (was 22%). Guidance after Q3: adjusted EPS at least $9.50 (was $9.00), which is ~0.94% pretax on $162bn; GAAP EPS at least $15.09 (was $6.52), but ~$7.50 of that is the Q4 non-cash put-liability reversal, so clean GAAP is ~$7.6 (~0.74% pretax). 9M clean pretax was $2.58bn (reported $2.76bn less $181m of other income) and Q4 is a seasonal loss (Q4 2025 net loss $781m). Base year-1 pretax 0.90% (was 0.85%) sits between the clean-GAAP and adjusted floors. FY2027 (re-judged, growth only): Humana sent non-renewal notices to ~600,000 MA members (~8% of the MA base) in plans rated 3.5 stars or below, with ~40% recapture expected, and CMS finalised only a ~2.48% average benchmark increase. Base FY2027 growth is cut from 6% to 2% (bull 8% to 4%, bear 3% to 0%). FY2027 margins are UNCHANGED (base 1.6%): the 2027 payment-year bonus was set by the Oct-2025 release (~20% of members in 4+ star plans), so 2027 improvement has to come from pricing and exits, which is what the prior path already assumed. STAR RATINGS (re-judged, FY2028+): the Oct-2026 release put ~93-95% of MA members in 4+ star plans for payment-year 2028. The prior base assumed only a partial H5216 recovery; base FY2028 pretax moves 2.5% to 2.8% and FY2029 2.9% to 3.0%. The 3.0% consolidated mid-cycle is UNCHANGED: the Stars result brings the recovery forward, it does not change what CMS rate-setting below cost trend allows the business to earn. Bull margin path UNCHANGED (it already assumed this outcome). The prior bear premise (H5216 misses again) is falsified, so the bear is redefined around structural cost trend, CMS rates and a later Stars reversal, with FY2028 pretax 2.0% (was 1.5%) and mid-cycle 2.2% (was 2.0%). DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, and what would move each: cost of equity 9% (a move of 50bp+ in the 10y UST); terminal growth and the 15x/16x/13x FCFE caps; 24% tax rate (a statutory change); SBC 0.19% of revenue; statutory capital retention at 5% of incremental revenue (management says reinsurance and entity restructuring cut 2026 capital contribution requirements by more than $3bn, which would make the modelled ~$1.6bn FY2026 retention too high, but reinsurance is paid for in margin and the FY2026 statutory filings are not yet available; a disclosed RBC ratio well above target at year-end would lower this); revenue growth from FY2028; base and bull mid-cycle margins (FY2027 guidance in February and the 2028 CMS rate notice would move them). Management's 2028 targets (MA pretax margin at least 3%, EPS $38-42) are still NOT adopted as base. Street basis (SBC as non-cash) sits ~$45/share above house: SBC is only 0.19% of revenue but the charge is ~$0.3-0.4bn/yr on this revenue base. The FCFE cap binds in all three scenarios (Gordon at 9%/3% would be 17x), so the sensitivity grid is flat at discount rates of 8% and below; the cap, not terminal growth, sets the terminal value.
inputs.capital_retention_note: wc_capture_pct = -5: for every $1 of incremental revenue, $0.05 of net income is retained as statutory capital in the regulated subsidiaries and is not distributable. The FY2026 revenue step-up (+$32bn) therefore consumes ~$1.6bn of FY2026 earnings, which is why year-1 FCFE is negative in all three scenarios and why buybacks have been token. Cross-check: state-regulated subsidiaries held $15.7bn of statutory capital and surplus at 30 Jun 2026, and consolidated equity rose $1.15bn in 9M 2026 against $2.0bn of net income.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward judgment: post-2026 revenue growth of 4-6% (Medicare-eligible population +3%/yr plus premium yield) corroborated by the 5.3% equity_5yr_cagr; neither the 11% trailing revenue CAGR (share gains as UNH/Aetna shrink footprint, not repeatable) nor the negative EPS/FCFE CAGRs (Stars trough) are a usable forward rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.9-5.3%) diverges by more than 30% from revenue (10.9-11.8%) and EPS (-17 to -24%). Revenue compounded on MA membership share gains while earnings collapsed on the H5216 Star Ratings loss and industry-wide MA margin compression; FY2025 EPS $9.87 is a trough, not a trend.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the FCFE proxy (net income less 5% of the revenue change), the series this model discounts: FY2020 $2,754m, FY2022 $2,316m, FY2025 $608m. Reported FCF (OCF - capex) CAGRs are shown for reference only: FY2025 reported FCF of $375m is CMS-timing noise, not economics. SBC-adjusted and reported series diverge by less than 0.2pp because SBC is 0.19% of revenue.

base.ebitda_margin_note: = pretax margin [0.90, 1.6, 2.8, 3.0, 3.0 ...] + sbc_pct 0.19. FY2026 between the clean-GAAP (~$7.6) and adjusted ($9.50) EPS floors; FY2027 repricing and plan exits with the Stars bonus still lost; FY2028 Stars bonus restored (93-95% of members in 4+ star plans); 3.0% consolidated pretax mid-cycle from 2029 (below management's 2028 target).
base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +25% on the nine-month run-rate, then +2% in FY2027 as ~600,000 MA members in low-rated plans are non-renewed (about 40% recaptured) against a 2.48% CMS benchmark increase, then 5% decaying to 3% terminal. Pretax margin troughs at 0.90% in FY2026, 1.6% in FY2027 with the Stars bonus still lost, recovers to 2.8% in FY2028 as the restored bonus arrives, and settles at 3.0% consolidated (MA ~3% plus CenterWell), which is mid-cycle for HUM post-V28. Cost of equity 9%, terminal 3%, 15x FCFE cap.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: = pretax margin [1.0, 2.0, 3.3, 3.7, 3.8 ...] + sbc_pct 0.19. Management's path: Stars bonus restored for payment-year 2028 (now confirmed), MA pretax margin at least 3% by 2028, EPS near the $38-42 range by 2028-2029 and 3.8% consolidated thereafter (still below the FY19-FY23 average of ~4.4%).
bull.narrative: The Stars recovery is now in hand; the bull additionally needs medical cost trend to keep moderating as value-based care delivers the inpatient favourability seen in 2026, and CMS rate notices to stop lagging trend. Revenue +4% in FY2027 on better-than-40% recapture of exited members, 7% in FY2028, then decaying; CenterWell scales through the capital-light BlackRock JV. Consolidated pretax reaches 3.8% by 2030, in line with management's 2028 EPS target of $38-42 delivered a year or two late. Same 9% cost of equity; 16x cap.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: = pretax margin [0.8, 1.0, 2.0, 2.2, 2.2 ...] + sbc_pct 0.19. The payment-year 2028 Stars bonus arrives (it is set), but CMS benchmark increases keep lagging 7-8% cost trend (double-digit drug trend, GLP-1s), a later Stars cut-point shift claws back part of the bonus, and DOJ FCA litigation adds cost; Humana settles at 2.2% consolidated pretax.
bear.narrative: The Stars bonus returns in 2028 but does not stick as earnings: CMS rate notices stay below medical and pharmacy cost trend, cut-point volatility takes back part of the bonus in later years, RADV audits and the DOJ broker-payment case (past a motion to dismiss) add cost, and the 2027 plan exits recapture fewer members than planned, leaving FY2027 revenue flat. Consolidated pretax margin recovers only to 2.2%, growth reverts to demographic 3%, terminal growth 2.5%, 13x cap. Year-1 FCFE is negative as the FY2026 revenue step-up consumes statutory capital at a 0.8% margin.

scenario_narratives.base: One more trough year, then the restored Star Ratings bonus lifts consolidated pretax margin to 2.8% in FY2028 and 3.0% from FY2029, which is mid-cycle for Humana in a post-V28 world where CMS rates run below cost trend. FY2026 revenue +25%, FY2027 only +2% as low-rated plans are exited, then 5% decaying to 3%. Near-term FCFE is roughly nil because the FY2026 revenue jump consumes ~$1.6bn of statutory capital; the value is in years 3-10 and the terminal.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management's plan delivered a year or two late: with Stars restored, cost trend also moderates on value-based care and CMS rates stop lagging; Humana recaptures most exited members and grows 4% in FY2027 and 7% in FY2028; consolidated pretax reaches 3.8% by 2030 (EPS around management's $38-42 target). Of the three things the bull needed (Stars, trend, CMS rates) one is delivered and one is running favourably.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2028 Stars bonus arrives but CMS benchmark increases keep lagging a 7-8% cost trend with double-digit drug inflation, later cut-point shifts claw back part of the bonus, RADV and the DOJ FCA case add cost, and FY2027 revenue is flat after the plan exits. Margin recovers only to 2.2%, growth reverts to demographics. No solvency question, but the business earns roughly FY2023 economics in perpetuity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from 25/50/25 to 20/50/30, part-way back to the 15/50/35 house default. The prior weights carried a 25% bear specifically because the Oct-2026 Star Ratings release was a pending binary event; it resolved decisively in Humana's favour (93-95% of MA members in 4+ star plans against ~20%), and the bull, which needed Stars, cost trend and CMS rates all to break favourably, now has the first delivered and the second running ahead of guidance in Q3. Not taken all the way to the default: earnings still depend on a single regulator, the 2027 benchmark increase of 2.48% lags cost trend, Stars cut-points have reversed before, and the DOJ False Claims Act case survived a motion to dismiss.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Humana is valued as an equity stream: net income after interest, less the equity retained for statutory capital as MA revenue grows, capitalised at a 9% cost of equity with no net-debt deduction (holding-company debt is charged through interest expense). The valuation neither extrapolates the FY2026 trough (adjusted EPS at least $9.50; the $15.09 GAAP floor is inflated by a non-cash put-liability reversal) nor adopts management's 2028 EPS target of $38-42; base settles at a 3.0% consolidated pretax margin from 2029, roughly two-thirds of Humana's FY2019-FY2023 average, reflecting structural CMS rate pressure. The October 2026 Star Ratings result removed the largest single risk to the recovery and shows up mainly in the scenario weights and in a milder bear case, since the base case had already assumed a recovery.
key_risks_to_valuation: Medical and pharmacy cost trend (7-8%, double-digit drug) proving structural rather than transitory, so repricing continually lags cost
CMS rate notices (2.48% average for 2027) and the V28 risk-model phase-in setting benchmarks below trend industry-wide; the 2028 rate notice is the next test
Star Ratings cut-point volatility: the 2027 ratings restore the payment-year 2028 bonus, but ratings are re-set every October and have swung both ways
2027 plan exits (~600,000 members): recapture well below the ~40% seen after the 2025 exits would cut revenue further than the +2% base assumes

Statutory capital retention on the 2026 membership surge (~5% of incremental revenue assumed) is a judgment; reinsurance and restructuring may have lowered the true requirement, while a capital contribution to subsidiaries would reduce distributable earnings further
DOJ False Claims Act broker-payment complaint (survived a motion to dismiss) and RADV audit exposure, which are not reserved in the margin paths
Terminal value is capped at 15x FCFE; the valuation is terminal-heavy because years 1-2 contribute almost no distributable cash
